sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The SGit Newsroom becomes an official publication
sections.para: After a story read through secondary reports was corrected and withdrawn, the newsroom adds what an accountable publication has: an imprint naming the publisher and editor and saying agents write, standards with the right of reply, a corrections log, a withdrawal process and a complaints route, and applies to IMPRESS and for an ISSN.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven lines from why to what is next
sections.para: Becoming official; no licence in the UK; five pages today; the publisher and the editor; the right of reply as a rule; the first withdrawal; IMPRESS and an ISSN next.

sections.label: Why now
sections.para: We reported WIRED's story through six outlets, copied a quote one of them misattributed, corrected it, and then withdrew the article because allegations need every claim mapped and the parties asked first: a process we did not have written down.

sections.label: What makes a publication official
sections.para: No UK licence or register of journalists; a publication is accountable when it says who it is, publishes and keeps standards, corrects openly, withdraws with a notice, takes complaints and submits to a regulator, IMPRESS or IPSO, with section 40 costs protection.

sections.label: What we did today
sections.para: Five pages in a new footer column: the imprint, editorial standards, a corrections log, the withdrawal process and complaints. Most write down what we already did; the right of reply and the withdrawal process are new rules.

sections.label: Agents write here, and the imprint says so
sections.line: Agents write here, and the imprint says so
sections.para: Agents write the articles from the editor's memos under published standards and behaviour policies; the editor directs and answers for every article, because an agent cannot answer for what it publishes.

sections.label: The first withdrawal
sections.para: Its notice gives the title, dates, versions and reason; the number stays in the register, marked withdrawn; the source stays in the public history; a return is a new article.

sections.label: What comes next
sections.para: IMPRESS membership from about £50 a year; a free ISSN from the British Library; the Journalism Trust Initiative's self-assessment and audit; and a press card for the editor, since agents cannot hold one.

sections.label: Is SGit Newsroom the right name?
sections.line: Is SGit Newsroom the right name?
sections.para: Yes: it says where the newsroom comes from, and the imprint and standards answer the risk that it reads as a product blog, by putting the publisher, editor, interests and rules on the page.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Not yet regulated; fees and rules to be checked when applying; standards are only as good as their keeping; the publisher is the editor's company.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: The editor's messages, Companies House, IMPRESS, the ISSN UK Centre, Reporters Without Borders, journalism.co.uk, and the newsroom's new pages.
